analysis.evidence: Abram is the subject of the opening verb. He went as YHWH had told him, and בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵחָרָן identifies the journey as his departure from Haran.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: go, move from place to place

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּלֶךְ אַבְרָם, “Abram went,” אַבְרָם names the subject of the verb. The verse repeats his name when giving his age at departure from Haran. Haqor indexes the name under אבה through its אָב (“father”) element.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Relative particle with prefixed comparative preposition כַּ.

analysis.evidence: כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֵלָיו יַהְוֶה means “as Yahweh had spoken to him.” אֵלָיו identifies Abram as the addressee, and כַּאֲשֶׁר links his departure to Yahweh’s earlier instruction.
analysis.morphology: Piel perfect, third person masculine singular, with יַהְוֶה as its subject.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּלֶךְ אִתּוֹ לוֹט, אִתּוֹ means “with him” and refers to Abram. Lot went with Abram.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Lot as its subject.

evidence.note: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.

article.name: לוֹט
article.summary: Terah’s genealogy names Lot as Haran’s son and Abram’s nephew. The passage gives no explanation of the name.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for לוֹט with its etymology unassigned.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:27 names Lot as the son whom Haran fathered.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּלֶךְ אִתּוֹ לוֹט, “Lot went with him,” לוֹט is the subject of וַיֵּלֶךְ. The pronoun in אִתּוֹ refers to Abram, whom Lot accompanies.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Haran’s son.

analysis.evidence: The verse first names Abram as the subject of וַיֵּלֶךְ, “he went.” After reporting that Lot went with him, וְאַבְרָם names Abram again as the man who was seventy-five when he left Haran.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ prefixes the masculine personal name אַבְרָם and introduces a clause stating Abram’s age.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: בֶּן introduces חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, five years plus seventy years, giving Abram’s age as seventy-five when he left Haran.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun governing the following expression of age.

In בֶּן חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים וְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, the conjunction joins ‘five years’ and ‘seventy years’ to give Abram’s age of seventy-five when he left Haran.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ prefixes a cardinal numeral in the plural absolute form, used with either gender.
Feminine singular absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מֵחָרָן names the place Abram left. The phrase בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵחָרָן tells when Abram was seventy-five years old.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ gives the Qal infinitive construct צֵאת temporal force. The third-person masculine singular suffix וֹ marks Abram as the subject.
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

draft.evidence: In בְּצֵאתוֹ מֵחָרָן, the preposition מֵ־ marks Haran as Abram’s point of departure.

analysis.evidence: בְּצֵאתוֹ means “when he went out.” The following מֵחָרָן identifies the place Abram left, the same Haran where his household had settled in Genesis 11:31.
analysis.morphology: The preposition מִן takes the form מֵ־ before the guttural ח of the place name חָרָן.
analysis.sense: Haran, the place from which Abram departed.
